lesson: Card #5 (one match, Estrela vs Braga) won: BTTS landed at 2-2, +$9.21. Small sample, but it's a reminder that a single well-researched pick on a quiet day beats forcing volume for its own sake. Today's the opposite problem — six genuine fixtures across six leagues — so the discipline that matters today is not letting a busy card turn into a bigger stake day than the picks actually justify.

matches.analysis: Valencia are winless in four (draw, two defeats, then thrashed 0-5 by Barcelona) and have failed to score in three of those four games. Sevilla, by contrast, have won two of their last three, including an away win at Athletic Bilbao. Model rates Sevilla 47% at home to Valencia's 24% — a clean form gap, not a reputation call.

Both sides are winless in their last three. Venezia have shipped 7 goals in that run; Fiorentina have scored just once in three games, including a 0-4 hammering at Roma. Backing Fiorentina here purely because they're the bigger name would be exactly the prestige-trap mistake this card tries to avoid — their current form gives no real case for it. Genuinely hard to trust either side. Pass.

Schalke held Bayern to a 0-0 draw last time out — a genuinely good defensive result — but they haven't scored a single goal in their last two league matches. Union Berlin's own defence has been shaky (four conceded at Leverkusen), but Schalke's toothless attack means Union's home advantage and superior model rating (40.9% to 32.2%) should be enough.

Rennes are unbeaten in three, including a very credible 2-2 draw away at PSG, plus two wins either side of it. Marseille have lost two of their last three, and the concerning one is a home defeat to newly-promoted Paris FC — a side they should be well clear of. Model gives Rennes a clear 46% to Marseille's 29%.

Mechelen are winless in five (two draws, three defeats), just lost 0-4 at home to Westerlo, and have the joint-worst attack and worst defence in the league. On top of that they're missing seven players to injury and absence for this match. Anderlecht haven't been prolific themselves, but they've conceded only five goals all season — the third-best defensive record in the division — which should be enough against a side this short-handed.

FEATURED MATCH. AZ are 5-0-0, top of the table, and have scored 16 goals in five games — more than any other side in the division — including going over 3.5 goals in four of those six games (Super Cup included). Willem II have taken one point from four, concede freely, and are missing their first-choice goalkeeper. AZ's straight win price is under 1.25 — far too short to be worth backing outright — but the goals market captures the same dominant form at a genuinely useful price. This is current form, not reputation: AZ finished only 7th last season.

West Ham sit top of the Championship, on a three-match winning streak with 15 goals scored in their last five — including the 3-2 win at Bolton already on our tracker. Wrexham have drawn four of their last six and have looked more solid than sharp. The price is short, but the underlying gap in current attacking output is real and specific, not just a reputation gap between a relegated Premier League side and a promoted one.
